repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until(not ((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true))
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR uses a rising-edge wait (`wait(MotionSensor.Motion == true, edge rising)`) which must block until the transition occurs. The candidate uses a periodic `if` guard evaluated only at body start. Evidence F2 shows the motion signal became true at t=100ms, but the JoI emitted no action because the guard was false at t=0 and the script did not block to wait for the edge.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with the required blocking rising-edge state machine: persist `fired` state, block on `not (C)` if previously fired, block on `C` if not fired, execute body, then mark fired. This ensures the action fires exactly when the signal transitions to true, matching the IR's rising-edge semantics.
